nindian-history-121-4.s: Who led the assault that recaptured Delhi from the rebels in 1857?
nindian-history-121-4.x: John Nicholson led the assault on Delhi; Hugh Rose took Jhansi, Colin Campbell relieved and recaptured Lucknow, and Henry Lawrence died defending the Lucknow Residency.

n3539c777c75.s: The Summary Revenue Settlement introduced in Awadh in 1856 was made directly with:
n3539c777c75.x: The 1856 settlement was made directly with village proprietors, while the taluqdars lost their estates, were disarmed and had their forts demolished.

nindian-history-121-11.s: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Bareilly?
nindian-history-121-11.x: Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly; Kunwar Singh led at Jagdishpur in Bihar, Ahmadullah Shah at Faizabad and Tatya Tope in Central India.

n4b63595111b.s: Which of the following book–author pairs on the Revolt of 1857 is NOT correctly matched?
o: Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies – S.B. Chaudhuri
The Peasant and the Raj – Rudrangshu Mukherjee
n4b63595111b.x: The Peasant and the Raj was written by Eric Stokes, not Rudrangshu Mukherjee, who wrote Awadh in Revolt 1857-58.

nindian-history-6-23.s: Who wrote 'The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857'?
nindian-history-6-23.x: R.C. Majumdar wrote The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857; Savarkar wrote The Indian War of Independence, 1857, Chaudhuri wrote Civil Rebellion in the Indian Mutinies and Ashok Mehta wrote 1857: The Great Rebellion.

nae7ebb956e7.s: The Meerut rising of the Revolt of 1857 began on:
nae7ebb956e7.x: The Meerut rising began on 10 May 1857; Mangal Pandey's action at Barrackpore was on 29 March and the 19th Native Infantry refused at Berhampur in February 1857.

n7d3bf87a7c1.s: After 1858, the British Crown's policy towards religion in India was one of:
n7d3bf87a7c1.x: After 1858 the Crown promised religious neutrality and withdrew state patronage from missionary work.

nba78509b598.s: According to Sir Syed Ahmed Khan, one cause of the Revolt of 1857 was:
o: Lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council
Complete equality between Indian and British soldiers
Excessive Indian representation in the Legislative Council
Too much British respect for Indian customs
nba78509b598.x: Sir Syed blamed the lack of Indian representation in the Legislative Council and the British misunderstanding of Indian customs; equality of soldiers was not a cause he identified.

nee264d593f2.s: The Inam Commission of 1852, which confiscated about 20,000 estates whose owners could not show title, was set up in:
nee264d593f2.x: The Inam Commission (1852) worked in Bombay, not Madras, and confiscated some 20,000 estates lacking title.

n758f58382b7.s: The General Service Enlistment Act, 1856 was passed under which Governor-General?
n758f58382b7.x: The Act was Canning's (1856); it required recruits to serve anywhere, including overseas, which orthodox Hindu sepoys feared would cost them caste.

n49e6fc86004.s: Which developments before 1857 generated fears of mass conversion among Indians?
o: Western education, railways and the telegraph
Ending of the Company's trade monopoly
n49e6fc86004.x: Western education, railways and the telegraph, along with missionaries preaching under police protection, created fears of mass conversion and loss of caste.

n86c858b41c5.s: Which of the following was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse before 1857?
n86c858b41c5.x: Satara (along with Jhansi and Nagpur) was annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse; Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance.

n5d73fe3cb2a.s: Which Nawab of Awadh was deposed when Awadh was annexed in 1856?
n5d73fe3cb2a.x: Wajid Ali Shah was deposed when Awadh was annexed in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance, costing lords, officials, retainers and soldiers their livelihoods.

n1705e5439c3.s: Before 1857, the lower courts and judicial system in British India generally favoured:
n1705e5439c3.x: Justice was slow, costly and corrupt and generally favoured the rich over the poor.

nindian-history-6-10.x: India Divided was written by Rajendra Prasad; Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj, My Experiments with Truth and Gokhale: My Political Guru.

nb42d532d491.s: Before the Revolt of 1857, mysterious chapatis were passed from village to village across:
nb42d532d491.x: The chapatis passed village to village across North India, not South India.

n10cc2dc95e6.x: Bhatta was the foreign service allowance; it was withdrawn for service in Sindh and Punjab once they became British territory.

n71c673bae4e.s: What was the slogan of the Meerut rebels when they marched in May 1857?
n71c673bae4e.x: After 85 sepoys of the 3rd (Light) Cavalry were jailed, the rebels freed the prisoners and marched to Delhi with the slogan 'Dilli Chalo'.

nfca0feedbb2.s: In 1857, Scindia of Gwalior, whose troops went over to the Rani, fled to:
nfca0feedbb2.x: Scindia stayed loyal to the British, but his troops defected to the Rani and he fled to Agra.

nbc3dcf6218e.s: Which Nizam of Hyderabad remained pro-British during the Revolt of 1857?
nbc3dcf6218e.x: Afzal-ud-Daula remained pro-British, and his loyalty helped keep the Deccan quiet.

n82452d90537.s: General Bakht Khan, the real military leader of the rebels at Delhi, came to Delhi from:
n82452d90537.x: Bakht Khan came from Bareilly, reaching Delhi on 3 July 1857, and led a 10-member 'Court of Soldiers' there.

n7c173235d15.s: Begum Hazrat Mahal of Lucknow declared whom the ruler of Awadh in 1857?
n7c173235d15.x: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt at Lucknow and proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr ruler of Awadh.

n3425ba6632b.s: Bareilly was recaptured by the British in:
n3425ba6632b.x: Bareilly was recaptured in May 1858, after Jhansi was retaken in April 1858.

n4d24e1326a5.s: After the fall of Delhi, Bahadur Shah Zafar was tried and exiled to:
n4d24e1326a5.x: Bahadur Shah Zafar was captured after Delhi fell, tried and exiled to Rangoon.

nindian-history-120-29.s: Tantia Tope led the Revolt of 1857 mainly in:
nindian-history-120-29.x: Tantia Tope operated in Central India; Kunwar Singh led in Bihar, Begum Hazrat Mahal in Awadh and Bakht Khan at Delhi.

n5ec415a5baf.s: Uda Devi fought against the British in 1857 at:
n5ec415a5baf.x: Uda Devi fought at Sikandar Bagh in Lucknow; Jhalkari Bai is linked with Jhansi and Azizun with Kanpur.

n2688f04b10c.x: Campbell retook Kanpur in December 1857 and Lucknow in March 1858; Hugh Rose took Jhansi in April and Gwalior in June 1858.

nindian-history-121-3.s: Who was Governor-General during the Revolt of 1857 and read out the Queen's Proclamation at Allahabad in 1858?
nindian-history-121-3.x: Lord Canning was Governor-General during the revolt and, as the first Viceroy, read out the Queen's Proclamation of 1858 at Allahabad.

n0358fd35b79.s: Which of the following was a major limitation of the Revolt of 1857?
o: Participation of all major princes and urban elites
Superior arms in the hands of the rebels
Lack of coordination and central leadership
n0358fd35b79.x: The revolt suffered from lack of coordination and central leadership; many big princes and urban elites stayed away, and the rebels had inferior arms and no unified programme.

nf6857fb5e5a.s: Which of the following pairs regarding 1857 is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Holkar of Indore – Supported the British
Bhonsle state of Nagpur – Joined the revolt under its ruling prince
Sikh chiefs of Patiala, Nabha and Jind – Actively helped the British
Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I – Kept the Deccan quiet
nf6857fb5e5a.x: Nagpur had already been annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse in 1854, so there was no ruling prince to join the revolt.

nc0540742bd7.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nc0540742bd7.s: Maulvi Ahmadullah led the Revolt of 1857 in:
nc0540742bd7.x: Ahmadullah operated in Faizabad; Khan Bahadur Khan was in Rohilkhand, Kunwar Singh in Bihar and Tantia Tope in Central India.

n44188679fc6.s: Which of the following was a reason for the failure of the Revolt of 1857?
n44188679fc6.x: The revolt lacked an all-India character and a unified nationalist programme; the rebels had inferior arms and poor communication.

n971bcad0514.s: The rebel attack on the Hyderabad Residency, which was repulsed, took place on:
n971bcad0514.x: The attack on the Hyderabad Residency on 17 July 1857 was repulsed, as the Nizam Afzal-ud-Daula and Salar Jung I stayed loyal.

na75373af7d5.s: Rani Lakshmibai died fighting near Gwalior on 17 June 1858 against the force of:
na75373af7d5.x: After capturing Gwalior with Tantia Tope, the Rani died near Gwalior fighting Sir Hugh Rose's force, not defending Jhansi against Campbell.

nda817aa3618.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the limitations of calling the Revolt of 1857 the First War of Independence?
o: There was no common goal among all participants
Modern nationalism had not yet emerged
The revolt spread evenly across the whole of India
nda817aa3618.x: The revolt did not spread evenly; it was confined largely to North India while most of India remained neutral.

nc63c5f87093.shape: one-liner (match not possible from the facts)
nc63c5f87093.s: The national character of the Revolt of 1857 is best described as:
o: A traditional uprising of different classes against a common foreign enemy
A modern nationalist movement with a common programme
nc63c5f87093.x: The idea of a single Indian nation-state had not yet emerged; different classes defended local, economic and religious interests against a common foreign enemy.

n57d3011929c.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n57d3011929c.s: Which of the following groups stayed loyal to the British during the Revolt of 1857?
n57d3011929c.x: The big zamindars of Bengal stayed loyal, while Awadh taluqdars and zamindars, and peasants and artisans of Awadh and western UP, joined the revolt.

n987adf86352.s: Which historian, emphasising local agrarian studies, viewed the Revolt of 1857 as a combination of several peasant and elite risings?
n987adf86352.x: Eric Stokes stressed local agrarian studies and saw the revolt as multiple peasant and elite risings, not one centrally directed movement.

nf909c2852fb.s: R.C. Majumdar and S.N. Sen regarded Indian nationalism in the mid-nineteenth century as:
nf909c2852fb.x: Both Majumdar and Sen regarded Indian nationalism in the mid-nineteenth century as still embryonic.

n3caadd62aeb.s: Who wrote 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven', the Government of India-commissioned centenary history of the revolt?
n3caadd62aeb.x: S.N. Sen's Eighteen Fifty-Seven was the official centenary history; R.C. Majumdar wrote his 1957 work independently after parting with the official project.

n08defbcc1a3.s: Who (with W. Taylor) described the Revolt of 1857 as a Muslim conspiracy exploiting Hindu grievances?
n08defbcc1a3.x: Outram saw it as a Muslim conspiracy exploiting Hindu grievances; Rees called it a war of fanatic religionists against Christians and Holmes a conflict between civilisation and barbarism.

nefc8e69b264.s: The Revolt of 1857 began as a ____ and rapidly developed into a popular rebellion.
nefc8e69b264.x: It began among soldiers as a mutiny but quickly drew in rulers, peasants and common people.

n42a44308a6a.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the reorganisation of the army after 1857?
o: Artillery and key positions were reserved for Europeans
Regiments were organised without regard to caste or region
Recruitment shifted towards groups described as martial races
Recruitment shifted from Awadh and Bihar towards Punjab, Gorkhas and the NWFP
n42a44308a6a.x: Under 'divide and counterpoise' regiments were deliberately mixed by caste and region, so those identities were not ignored.

n25d1791ffd1.s: Which of the following pairs about the Telugu regions after the establishment of Crown rule is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Coastal Andhra – Part of the Madras Presidency
Rayalaseema – Part of the Madras Presidency
Telangana – Separate province administered directly from London
Nizam's dominions – Subject to British suzerainty
n25d1791ffd1.x: Telangana remained under the Nizam, subject to British suzerainty; it was not a province administered from London.

n82a127aa516.s: The Queen's Proclamation of 1858 promised that appointments to public service would be made on the basis of:
n82a127aa516.x: It promised appointment by merit and qualifications without discrimination of race or creed, and that Company treaties with the princes would be honoured.

n1d08ba803ae.s: After 1857, Indian princes were assured their states would not ordinarily be annexed, provided they accepted:
o: Direct rule by the Board of Control
n1d08ba803ae.x: The princes kept their states subject to British paramountcy and became subordinate allies of the Crown.

n6ae2d3addfc.s: After 1858, the head of the Government of India was styled 'Viceroy' in relation to:
n6ae2d3addfc.x: The same office-holder was Viceroy in relation to the princely states and Governor-General in British India.

o: The treaties made by the Company
nfa90aeefa71.x: The Proclamation disclaimed further annexation of Indian States and placed the administration of India under the Crown.

nca62e26cd59.s: The Council of India created by the Government of India Act, 1858 to advise the Secretary of State had how many members?
nca62e26cd59.x: The Council of India consisted of 15 members and advised the Secretary of State for India.

nd7d7c0625c6.s: The Madras Native Association (1852) was founded by:
nd7d7c0625c6.x: Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty's Madras Native Association (1852) was the first to petition against non-implementation of the Allahabad Proclamation.

n81e5d3c7156.s: The rebels of 1857 proclaimed Bahadur Shah II as:
n81e5d3c7156.x: The rebels proclaimed him Shahenshah-e-Hindustan; he was later tried and exiled to Rangoon, formally ending Mughal rule.

n53afd81a76b.s: The period 1858-1885, when the Queen's Proclamation's promise of equal employment was not kept, is called the:
n53afd81a76b.x: 1858-1885 is the 'Era of Broken Promises': the ICS stayed European-dominated, Secretary of State Kimberley saying an adequate number 'shall always be Europeans'.

n90955a8e0c6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the palegar risings in Rayalaseema?
o: The 1846 rising was led jointly by about 80 palegars
Thomas Munro was associated with suppressing the 1800–01 rising
The 1846 rising was the last major palegar rising before 1857
n90955a8e0c6.x: About 80 palegars were involved in 1800–01; the 1846 rising was a single-leader guerrilla revolt with a peasant and tribal base.

nfac2df10c50.s: Mutakuri Goudappa, who attacked the Sub-Collector's office at Taranikallu in 1801, was captured and hanged by:
nfac2df10c50.x: Goudappa was captured and hanged by Sub-Collector Dhakar, not by Collector Thomas Munro.

nd59a0261c35.s: Who assassinated Vijayarama Raju of Vizianagaram in his camp after the fall of Bobbili?
nd59a0261c35.x: After Vijayarama Raju, with Bussy's support, took Bobbili from Ranga Rao, Tandra Paparayudu assassinated him in his camp.

n204bc2db840.s: After the British seized the Vizianagaram fort on 2 August 1793, the Raja was ordered to live at:
n204bc2db840.x: The Raja was ordered to live in Machilipatnam, not Bobbili, after refusing the Rs 3 lakh tribute and disbanding of troops.

n82e0784e362.s: Military action to suppress the Palegars continued for about:
n82e0784e362.x: Suppression combined disarmament proclamations, eighteen months of military action, confiscation of rebel estates and small pensions for loyal heirs.

n4258ffa5e34.s: Before Vizianagaram was restored to him after the Battle of Padmanabham, the minor son Narayana Babu had hidden at:
n4258ffa5e34.x: Narayana Babu had hidden at Makkuva; the estate, reduced to an ordinary zamindari, was restored on accepting the Permanent Settlement (1802) and a Rs 6 lakh peshkash.

ne5ff4a76ae4.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy was the maternal grandson of:
ne5ff4a76ae4.x: He was the younger son of Pedda Mallareddy, Palegar of Uyyalawada, and the maternal grandson of Nosam Palegar Jayarama Reddy.

na73d5cdf80f.s: Which of the following explains the limited response to the Revolt of 1857 in Andhra?
o: Andhra had no local leaders at all
The Nizam had joined the revolt
Andhra was administered directly from London
Many preferred the stability of Company rule to the earlier anarchy
na73d5cdf80f.x: Many preferred Company stability to the earlier anarchy, and loyalty meetings were held at Visakhapatnam, Rajahmundry and Vijayawada; local leaders such as Korukonda Subba Reddy did exist.

ndcabf206756.s: The Nizam ceded Cuddapah, Kurnool, Anantapur and Bellary to the Company in:
ndcabf206756.x: The Ceded Districts were handed over in 1800 under the Subsidiary Alliance of 1798; Guntur had been taken in 1788 for Rs 7 lakh.

nd2edde29cde.s: Mir Turab Ali Khan, the Diwan of Hyderabad during 1857, is better known as:
nd2edde29cde.x: Afzal-ud-Daula, who succeeded Nasir-ud-Daula on 16 May 1857, retained Mir Turab Ali Khan (Salar Jung I) as Diwan; both were pro-British.

n074776ff984.s: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy was hanged on:
n074776ff984.x: The Faujdari Adalat sentenced him to death in January 1847 and he was hanged on 22 February 1847.

n091a954cb32.s: Turrebaz Khan, who led the attack on the Hyderabad Residency in 1857, was later caught and shot near:
n091a954cb32.x: After Resident Davidson repulsed the attack, Turrebaz Khan escaped but was caught and shot near Toopran (1859).

nac6331d9898.s: Which unit of the Hyderabad Contingent came under suspicion and was disarmed at Aurangabad in June 1857?
nac6331d9898.x: The 1st Cavalry of the Hyderabad Contingent was suspected and disarmed at Aurangabad; Mir Fida Ali was hanged.

nb3b9f3b2604.s: The Rampa rebellion of 1879 in the East Godavari Agency was an uprising of the:
nb3b9f3b2604.x: The 1879 Rampa rising was a Koya uprising against forest and toddy restrictions affecting podu cultivation.

n99e30384772.s: Korukonda Subba Reddy's rising in the Godavari Agency was influenced by rumours about the army of:
n99e30384772.x: Subba Reddy, operating at Errannagudem, was influenced by rumours of Nana Saheb's army; he was captured and executed.

nf3b7a2a4bea.s: The Nawabs of Kurnool, descended from Golconda nobles, were reduced and deposed in:
nf3b7a2a4bea.x: The Kurnool Nawabs were reduced and deposed in 1839.

n421d34384bf.x: Kattabomman was hanged in 1799; the Marudu brothers were executed in 1801.

nbc699f9ab48.s: The leader of the 1846 revolt was captured on 7 October 1846 at:
nbc699f9ab48.x: He was captured at the Jagannatha Swamy temple, Pairamalla Konda; Mundlapadu was the ambush site and Rudravaram and Koilakuntla were looted.

n808896f7732.s: Mubariz-ud-Daula of Hyderabad was arrested in:
n808896f7732.x: Mubariz-ud-Daula was arrested in 1839, long before the Aurangabad outbreak and the Residency attack of 1857.

nap-history-12-3.s: After the Battle of Tallikota (1565), the capital of Vijayanagara shifted to:
nap-history-12-3.x: Vijayanagara's defeat at Tallikota in 1565 led to the capital moving to Penugonda.

nap-history-12-22.s: The Battle of Chandurthi (1758), in which the English defeated the French, was fought for:
nap-history-12-22.x: The English beat the French at Chandurthi in 1758 in the struggle for the Northern Circars.

n1a7c1fb0d7a.s: Who renamed the Brahmo Sabha as the Brahmo Samaj?
n1a7c1fb0d7a.x: Debendranath Tagore renamed it; Rammohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828 with Dwarkanath Tagore.

n72376b0bd9b.s: M.G. Ranade founded the National Social Conference in 1887 along with:
n72376b0bd9b.x: Ranade founded the National Social Conference in 1887 with Raghunath Rao; it was the social wing of the Congress sessions.

n033ed4d00f8.s: Raja Rammohan Roy protested against the press curbs imposed by the Press Ordinance of:
n033ed4d00f8.x: Rammohan Roy protested the Press Ordinance of 1823 and also demanded fixed maximum rents for peasants.

n159d2456e24.s: Raja Rammohan Roy's Vedanta College, which blended Indian and Western learning, was founded in:
n159d2456e24.x: Vedanta College was founded in 1825 to blend Indian and Western learning.

n67fd300eaa9.s: Which of the following is classed as a revivalist movement?
n67fd300eaa9.x: The Arya Samaj (like Deoband) is classed as revivalist, whereas the Brahmo and Prarthana Samaj were reformist movements based on reason.

nindian-history-58-14.s: Who led the Tattvabodhini Sabha within the Brahmo movement?
nindian-history-58-14.x: Debendranath Tagore led the Tattvabodhini Sabha and the Brahmo movement.

n30b6b7a4b07.s: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj was formed in:
n30b6b7a4b07.x: The Sadharan Brahmo Samaj came in 1878; the Brahmo Samaj of India was formed in 1866, the Prarthana Samaj in 1867 and the Paramahansa Mandali in 1849.

nindian-history-120-24.x: Shiv Narayan Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj.

n81b60bf799a.s: The earliest Prarthana Samaj centre in Andhra was set up at Rajahmundry in 1878 by:
n81b60bf799a.x: Veeresalingam set up the first Andhra Prarthana Samaj centre at Rajahmundry in 1878; the Samaj itself was founded in 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang.

o: The authority of a single scripture
n7a30fe0a970.x: The Brahmo Samaj believed in one formless, eternal God, rejected avatars and treated no scripture as final authority.

nf192ff4d536.s: The orthodox Dharma Sabha, founded in 1830 to oppose the ban on Sati, was set up by:
nf192ff4d536.x: Raja Radhakant Deb founded the Dharma Sabha (1830) against Brahmo propaganda and the Sati ban that Rammohan Roy campaigned for.

n88c5f72943b.s: Which of the following was banned in the halls of the Brahmo Samaj?
n88c5f72943b.x: Idols and animal sacrifice were banned in Brahmo halls; it rejected priestly ritualism and caste and practised collective prayer.

n600d76b30a1.s: The Bengal Sati Regulation of 4 December 1829 was passed under Governor-General:
n600d76b30a1.x: It was passed under Lord William Bentinck and extended to Madras and Bombay in 1830.

na38b8a8cf9c.s: The Native Marriage Act of 1872, which legalised inter-caste marriage, is also known as the:
na38b8a8cf9c.x: The Native Marriage Act (Act III of 1872), also called the Brahmo Marriage Act, legalised inter-caste marriage and fixed minimum marriage ages.

nafd12c9867b.s: Among the following reformers, whose major contributions came earliest?
nafd12c9867b.x: The chronological order is Rammohan Roy, Vidyasagar, Jyotiba Phule and Dayanand Saraswati.

n844188b51ab.x: Rammohan Roy, who knew Persian, Arabic, Sanskrit and English, died at Bristol in 1833.

nf4a7508b77b.s: While respecting the traditional philosophies of the East, Raja Rammohan Roy wanted Indians to adopt:
o: A rejection of all Eastern thought
nf4a7508b77b.x: He drew on the Upanishads and Vedanta while standing for a rational, scientific approach.

nindian-history-97-11.x: Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission; the Prarthana Samaj is linked with Atmaram Pandurang and Ranade.

nc4fc9e3dc94.s: Keshab Chandra Sen introduced the Nava Vidhan in:
nc4fc9e3dc94.x: Keshab became Acharya in 1862, formed the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866, founded the Indian Reform Association in 1870 and introduced Nava Vidhan in 1880–81.

nindian-history-51-37.x: The Ramakrishna Mission was non-political, non-sectarian and humanitarian; Vivekananda joined pure Vedanta with the truth of all religions.

nindian-history-51-53.s: Ramakrishna Paramahamsa regarded Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ as:
o: Different names for the same God
nindian-history-51-53.x: He saw them as names of one God because he taught the unity behind all religions.

n4977408eb5d.x: The Brahmo Samaj opposed polygamy and child marriage and supported widow remarriage, women's education and women's property rights.

nf3cb2a713ee.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the reform movements of western and eastern India?
o: Satyashodhak Samaj focused on anti-Brahmanical reform and the uplift of lower castes
Prarthana Samaj was influenced by the Brahmo Samaj but followed a milder approach
Young Bengal represented a radical reform tendency
Paramahansa Mandali functioned as an open public organisation
nf3cb2a713ee.x: The Paramahansa Mandali functioned as a secret organisation, not an open one.

nindian-history-95-8.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nindian-history-95-8.s: The main aim of the Bhoodan Movement was to:
nindian-history-95-8.x: Bhoodan sought to give land to the landless; making Congress radical was the Workers and Peasants Party's aim and breaking unjust laws was Civil Disobedience.

o: Secret society that believed in one God
n707ee5f8410.x: It was a secret society believing in one God; its members broke caste rules and supported women's education and widow remarriage.

n00e516b5048.s: According to M.G. Ranade, social reform and religious reform should:
o: Be left entirely to the state
n00e516b5048.x: Ranade held that rigid religious belief obstructed progress and that social and religious reform were interrelated and should go together.

nd9aad66ebc1.s: The Prarthana Samaj pursued its reform agenda mainly through:
nd9aad66ebc1.x: It worked through persuasion and social work; its aims included raising the age of marriage and uplift of the depressed classes.

n2470cfc8e41.s: The National Social Conference met at the same time and place as the sessions of the:
n2470cfc8e41.x: Founded in 1887 by Ranade with Raghunath Rao, it met alongside the Congress sessions to discuss social reform.

n22df1569d82.s: Henry Vivian Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in:
n22df1569d82.x: Derozio was dismissed from Hindu College in 1831 and died the same year.

nindian-history-95-6.s: Which organisation sought to make the Congress more revolutionary and to organise the common people?
nindian-history-95-6.x: The Workers and Peasants Party sought a more radical Congress; the Radhasoami Satsang stressed one God, the Guru, Satsang and spiritual life.

nc07545803c7.s: Unlike the Brahmo Samaj, the Prarthana Samaj:
o: Required its members to leave Hindu society
Did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste practices
nc07545803c7.x: The Prarthana Samaj focused mainly on social reform and did not outright forbid idol worship or abandon caste as the Brahmos did.

n5e09308b603.s: Pandita Ramabai's Sharada Sadan was a:
n5e09308b603.x: Sharada Sadan was a home for widows; the secret society against caste was the Paramahansa Mandali.

n64e6ee0a0ad.s: The Deccan Education Society was founded at Pune by Tilak, Agarkar and Chiplunkar, with Ranade's support, in:
n64e6ee0a0ad.x: The Deccan Education Society was founded in Pune in 1884 with M.G. Ranade's support.

n3a0716f5c76.s: The Young Bengal Movement stood for:
o: Loyalty to idol worship and caste
Radical rationalism and criticism of social orthodoxy
n3a0716f5c76.x: Young Bengal stood for radical rationalism, opposed idol worship, casteism and decadent customs, and supported women's rights and education.

n4048e7db62a.shape: one-liner (match not possible from the facts)
n4048e7db62a.s: Which of the following was rejected by the Ten Principles of the Arya Samaj?
n4048e7db62a.x: The Ten Principles emphasised truth, rational thought, moral conduct and the welfare of all; the Arya Samaj rejected caste based on birth.

nbbe0916e50e.s: The Shuddhi movement, to reconvert those who had converted to Islam or Christianity, was started by the:
nbbe0916e50e.x: Shuddhi was started by the Arya Samaj to reconvert converts and admit outsiders into the Hindu fold.

n178be40ead2.s: Who called Dayananda Saraswati the 'Martin Luther of India'?
n178be40ead2.x: Lala Lajpat Rai gave him the title; Dayananda gave the slogan 'India for the Indians' and is credited with first using the term Swaraj.

nbd9ea9b7db6.x: He died at Ajmer; Lahore was only the later headquarters of the Arya Samaj, and his guru Virajananda was of Mathura.

nb65abb1cd54.s: Which organisation came to be regarded as a 'nursery of militant nationalists', influencing Lala Lajpat Rai and Swami Shraddhanand?
nb65abb1cd54.x: The Arya Samaj influenced Lala Lajpat Rai, Swami Shraddhanand and Bhagat Singh's family, earning this description.

n5bbef67d4ec.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
o: Salvation was possible only through renunciation and never through devotion
'As many faiths, so many paths' means all religions lead to the same truth
Salvation could be pursued through devotion, meditation and renunciation
Hari, Ram, Allah and Christ are different names for the same God
n5bbef67d4ec.x: Devotion was itself one of his paths to salvation, alongside meditation and renunciation, so it was not excluded.

ndf8eccdcdd8.s:
Assertion (A): The Indian headquarters of the Theosophical Society is at Adyar.
Reason (R): The Theosophical Society was originally founded at Madras in 1875.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ndf8eccdcdd8.x: Adyar became the Indian headquarters in 1882, so A is true; the Society was originally founded at New York, not Madras, so R is false.

nindian-history-127-20.s: The motto 'Atmano Mokshartham Jagad Hitaya Cha' belongs to the:
nindian-history-127-20.x: It is the Ramakrishna Mission's motto; the Theosophical Society stood for universal brotherhood and the Servants of India Society for constitutional service.

nae0896cbdbf.s: Which of the following forms part of the practical work of the Ramakrishna Mission?
nae0896cbdbf.x: The Mission runs schools, colleges, hospitals and orphanages and provides famine and disaster relief; its work is not exclusively ritualistic.

nd3f278dd816.s: The Arya Samaj regarded idol worship as:
nd3f278dd816.x: The Arya Samaj considered idol worship useless; it opposed caste by birth and held that all people could read the Vedas.

n267a3b0c261.x: Vivekananda was born Narendranath Datta in Calcutta on 12 January 1863; Gadadhar Chattopadhyaya was Ramakrishna's birth name.

nindian-history-127-5.s: 'Go Back to the Vedas' was the call of the:
nindian-history-127-5.x: The Arya Samaj said 'Go Back to the Vedas'; the Brahmo Samaj stood for worship of one God and the Theosophical Society for universal brotherhood.

nindian-history-14-29.s: The foundation stone of Banaras Hindu University, founded by Madan Mohan Malviya, was laid in:
nindian-history-14-29.x: BHU's foundation stone was laid in 1916; Annie Besant, whose Central Hindu School became its nucleus, cooperated in setting it up.

naca1fe89e5b.s: Who represented Jainism at the Chicago Parliament of Religions?
naca1fe89e5b.x: Virchand Gandhi represented Jainism; Mozoomdar the Brahmo Samaj, Dharmapala Buddhism (Ceylon) and Vivekananda Hinduism.

n637d2bcb3a2.s: Which of the following were core beliefs of the Theosophical Society?
n637d2bcb3a2.x: Karma and reincarnation were core beliefs; the Society drew on the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga and Vedanta and condemned child marriage.

n86ff7c92673.s: Annie Besant became the first woman President of the Indian National Congress at the session held at:
n86ff7c92673.x: She presided over the 1917 Calcutta Congress; she had launched the Home Rule movement in 1916 and ran New India and Commonweal.

nfac03bf1313.s: The split in the Arya Samaj over Western versus Vedic education and diet took place in:
nfac03bf1313.x: The split came in 1893, after Dayanand's death; 1875 is the founding year of the Arya Samaj at Bombay.

nindian-history-132-3.x: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj, Rammohan Roy the Brahmo Samaj and Dayanand the Arya Samaj.

n223e36ed5c7.s: Swami Vivekananda is described as the:
n223e36ed5c7.x: Vivekananda is called the 'Prophet of Indian Nationalism' and the 'Maker of Modern India'; the other titles belong to other personalities.

nf39ade3af71.s: The College (DAV) party of the Arya Samaj was led by Lala Hansraj and:
nf39ade3af71.x: The DAV party was led by Lala Hansraj and Lala Lajpat Rai; the Gurukul party by Swami Shraddhanand and Pandit Lekh Ram.

n447d7d2a209.s: Swami Vivekananda regarded humanitarian relief as:
o: The duty of the state alone
n447d7d2a209.x: Vivekananda regarded humanitarian relief as a monastic duty, condemned caste discrimination and condemned empty ritual.

nindian-history-126-5.s: Who founded the Manav Dharma Sabha?
nindian-history-126-5.x: Durgaram Manchharam founded the Manav Dharma Sabha; Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha and Agnihotri the Dev Samaj.

n014f3ef022d.s: Gurukul Kangri, which followed a traditional Vedic curriculum, was established at Haridwar in:
n014f3ef022d.x: Gurukul Kangri was set up at Haridwar in 1902 by the Gurukul party of Swami Shraddhanand and Pandit Lekh Ram.

nindian-history-116-6.x: Rammohan Roy founded the Atmiya Sabha; Atmaram Pandurang founded the Prarthana Samaj and Shiv Dayal Sahab the Radha Swami Satsang.

nindian-history-126-16.s: Which of the following was founded in 1875, the same year as the Arya Samaj?
nindian-history-126-16.x: The Theosophical Society was founded at New York in 1875; the Satyashodhak Samaj dates to 1873 and the Prarthana Samaj to 1867.

nindian-history-126-10.s: Modern education among Muslims was the aim of the:
nindian-history-126-10.x: Modern education among Muslims was the Aligarh Movement's aim, not the Dev Samaj's; Seva Sadan worked for women's welfare.

nindian-history-116-18.s: Vinoba Bhave was associated with the:
nindian-history-116-18.x: Vinoba Bhave led the Sarvodaya Samaj; Agnihotri founded the Dev Samaj and Phule the Satyashodhak Samaj.

nindian-history-132-6.s: The Servants of India Society was founded at Poona in 1905 by:
nindian-history-132-6.x: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society at Poona in 1905.

nindian-history-116-10.s: The Manav Dharma Sabha was founded in 1844 at:
nindian-history-116-10.x: The Manav Dharma Sabha was founded at Surat in 1844; the Nadwah-ul-Ulama was founded at Lucknow in 1894.

nindian-history-116-22.s: Jyotiba Phule's Satyashodhak Samaj was based at:
nindian-history-116-22.x: The Satyashodhak Samaj was based at Pune in Maharashtra; the Arya Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1875.

nbebbf5ced15.s: After 1857, Sayyid Ahmad Khan (1817-1898) promoted the modernisation of Muslims mainly through:
nbebbf5ced15.x: He promoted English education and a rational reading of Islam; his earlier thought had also included Hindu-Muslim unity.

n2e717b4a6d0.s: Who gave the Deoband movement political content, leading to the Jamiat-ul-Ulema?
n2e717b4a6d0.x: Mahmud-ul-Hasan gave Deoband political content; Shibli Numani founded the Nadwat al-Ulama at Lucknow and wanted English and European science taught.

n4a4f59c171f.s: The Scientific Society, founded by Sayyid Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur in 1864, was later shifted to:
n4a4f59c171f.x: The Society, which translated Western science, history and philosophy into Urdu, was later shifted to Aligarh, not Lucknow.

n84a5a5dd0cf.s: The Indian founder of the Wahabi Movement was:
n84a5a5dd0cf.x: The movement was named after Abdul Wahab of Arabia, but its Indian founder was Syed Ahmad Barelvi; it was crushed through the Ambala (1864) and Patna (1865) trials.

n570decc5113.s: The Deoband Movement, led by orthodox ulema, began at Deoband in which district?
n570decc5113.x: It began at Deoband in Saharanpur district of the United Provinces and opposed foreign rule.

n34313ea63d5.s: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental school, begun at Aligarh in 1875, was elevated into a college in:
n34313ea63d5.x: The MAO school began in 1875 and became a college in 1877 under Sayyid Ahmad Khan; Theodore Beck was later its principal, not its founder.

n6fd3b4e5a7d.s: Sayyid Ahmad Khan established the Muhammadan Educational Conference in:
n6fd3b4e5a7d.x: The Scientific Society came in 1864, the MAO school in 1875, the Muhammadan Educational Conference in 1886 and the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.

nbc28289e8de.s: Which movement helped build a modern educated Muslim middle class?
nbc28289e8de.x: Aligarh built a modern educated Muslim middle class, while Deoband kept alive an orthodox and anti-colonial strand.

nc13e0cbd033.s: To counter the Indian National Congress, Sayyid Ahmad Khan formed in 1888 the:
nc13e0cbd033.x: He advised Muslims to stay away from the Congress and formed the United Indian Patriotic Association in 1888.

n4e048795b0e.s: The Aligarh institution, begun as a school in 1875, became Aligarh Muslim University in:
n4e048795b0e.x: The school began in 1875, college classes in 1877, and it became Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

n60938e3e3f7.s: Unlike the Aligarh Movement, the Deoband Movement emphasised:
o: Western education and loyalty to the British
Traditional Islamic learning and opposition to foreign rule
n60938e3e3f7.x: Aligarh promoted Western education and loyalty to the British, while Deoband upheld traditional Islamic learning and opposed foreign rule.

nba087c09a23.s: Which of the following pairs relating to the Kuka movement is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Bhagat Jawahar Mal – Began the movement in the 1840s
Baba Ram Singh – Organised it as the Namdhari movement in 1857
Centre under Baba Ram Singh – Nankana Sahib
nba087c09a23.x: Under Baba Ram Singh the Kuka centre was at Bhaini, Ludhiana; Nankana Sahib is linked with the 1921 Akali massacre.

n83ff17e822d.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: too few dated facts)
n83ff17e822d.s: Shiv Dayal Singh (Soamiji Maharaj) founded the Radhasoami Satsang at Agra in:
n83ff17e822d.x: The Radhasoami Satsang was founded at Agra in 1861 and stressed inner realisation through the guru; 1830 is the Dharma Sabha of Radhakant Deb.

naf3f3898f75.s: Rast Goftar ('Truth-teller'), edited by Dadabhai Naoroji, was the organ of the:
naf3f3898f75.x: Rast Goftar was the Parsi reform paper of the Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha, not a Sikh paper.

n4b8b1c4f848.s: Which movement in Punjab advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system?
n4b8b1c4f848.x: The Kuka movement advocated boycott of British goods, English education, law courts and the postal system.

na833348201c.s: After the 1872 Malerkotla clash, the Kuka leader Baba Ram Singh was deported to:
na833348201c.x: Dozens of Kukas were blown from cannons and Ram Singh was deported to Rangoon in Burma.

nd53c6db5fd8.s: Which Sikh movement grew by cooperating with the British and became a separate group within Sikhism?
nd53c6db5fd8.x: The Nirankari movement grew by cooperating with the British and later became a separate group within Sikhism.

ndd3a1bb042a.s:
Assertion (A): Bhagya Reddy Varma was the President of the first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha.
Reason (R): Guduru Ramachandra Rao was the organiser of the first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
ndd3a1bb042a.x: Both are true: Bhagya Reddy Varma presided and Guduru Ramachandra Rao organised the Sabha, but one person's role as organiser does not explain another's presidency.

n61317a81b08.s: The 1917 resolution of the first Adi-Andhra session sought to replace the term 'Panchama' in Hyderabad by:
n61317a81b08.x: It sought 'Adi Andhra' in the Madras region and 'Adi Hindu' in Hyderabad, along with schools, wells in Dalit wadas and seats in local bodies and councils.

na30872ff693.s: Who sought the annihilation of caste, legal rights and separate electorates for the depressed classes?
na30872ff693.x: Ambedkar sought caste annihilation, legal rights and separate electorates, whereas Gandhi saw varna as a division of labour and untouchability as a corruption.

ne790c0bc54d.s: In 1925 Periyar broke with the Congress over communal representation and caste segregation at:
ne790c0bc54d.x: Periyar, who had been president and secretary of the provincial Congress, left in 1925 over communal representation and the Cheranmadevi Gurukulam segregation.

nb8d502dde8c.s: The Mahad Satyagraha led by B.R. Ambedkar asserted the right to draw water from:
nb8d502dde8c.x: Mahad concerned the right to draw water from the Chavdar tank in Maharashtra; Vaikom, in Travancore, concerned access to roads around a temple.

nb342f8e7c72.s: From 1920, the Justice Party formed the government in Madras how many times?
nb342f8e7c72.x: The Justice Party formed the government four times from 1920, won reservations for non-Brahmins and declined by 1937.

n145fdd432b6.s: The first Adi-Andhra session (first Provincial Panchama Mahajana Sabha) of November 1917 was held at:
n145fdd432b6.x: It met at Mailavaram Rajayya Nataka Mandir, Vijayawada, on 4-6 November 1917; the second conference was at Machilipatnam in 1919 and Amalapuram hosted the 1921 Sadassu.

n332c12a8676.s: The Justice Party lost power to the Congress in the elections of:
n332c12a8676.x: Weakened by lack of a mass base, Andhra–Tamil rifts and the deaths of Theagaraya Chetty and the Raja of Panagal, it lost to the Congress in 1937.

n980d182bda5.s: The Communal G.O. of 1921, regarded as a forerunner of reservation policy in South India, was secured by:
o: Intermediate landed castes of the non-Brahmin movement
n980d182bda5.x: It was secured by the intermediate landed castes of the non-Brahmin movement and was not meant exclusively for Dalit organisations.

na843e14cb98.s: The Justice Party's English newspaper 'Justice' began publication in:
na843e14cb98.x: Justice began in February 1917; the party, linked with the South India Peoples Association, was founded by T.M. Nair, P. Theagaraya Chetty and C. Natesa Mudaliar.

nbd0929439ee.s: The Arundhatiya Yuvajana Sangham worked for the welfare of the:
nbd0929439ee.x: The Arundhatiya Yuvajana Sangham was the organisation for Madiga welfare in Andhra.

nec644eaacd4.s: Gora founded the Atheist Centre in 1940 at:
nec644eaacd4.x: Gora founded the Atheist Centre at Mudunuru in 1940; it moved to Vijayawada in 1947.

na354e89a9c8.s: Panagal Raja, President of the Justice Party, served as Premier of Madras from:
na354e89a9c8.x: Panagal Raja was Premier from 1921 to 1926, was associated with Andhra University in 1926 and died on 16 December 1928.

n7ceceb0b903.s: Who was the first Chancellor of Andhra University?
n7ceceb0b903.x: Lord Goschen was the first Chancellor; A.P. Patro, as Education Minister, drove the 1926 Act, and the first headquarters was at Bezawada.

n77b545c26c9.s: Brahmins constituted approximately what share of the Madras Presidency's population?
n77b545c26c9.x: Brahmins were about 3 per cent of the population though they held over 90 per cent of government jobs.

na354c754420.s: In the 1920s, the Justice Party introduced:
na354c754420.x: The Justice Party introduced a caste-based roster, supported temple entry and promoted schools and scholarships for non-Brahmins.

n78da526a84a.s: The demand for reserved seats for non-Brahmins in the Andhra Mahasabha was echoed by Ponaka Pattabhirama Reddy and:
n78da526a84a.x: Pattabhirama Reddy and Tripuraneni Ramaswamy Chowdary echoed the demand; Gora and Periyar belong to other rationalist and anti-caste strands.

n5c84255a1cd.s: The Poona Pact, which replaced separate electorates with reserved seats in joint electorates, was signed on:
n5c84255a1cd.x: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 and gave 148 seats in place of the 71 under the Communal Award.

n41b62c05f12.s: The non-Brahmin movement in the Madras Presidency sought to end Brahmin dominance in:
n41b62c05f12.x: The movement aimed to end Brahmin dominance in jobs, education, politics and religion.

n03ada81f327.s: The All India Adi Hindu Conference at Lucknow in 1930, which chose Ambedkar as Dalit representative for the Round Table Conferences, was presided over by:
n03ada81f327.x: Bhagya Reddy Varma presided over the 1930 Lucknow conference.

n70756f65fd0.s: Self-respect marriages promoted by the Self-Respect Movement were conducted:
n70756f65fd0.x: Self-respect marriages were conducted without priests; the movement attacked caste hierarchy and priests and supported women's equality and property rights.

n39b258d6922.s: The DMK was formed on 17 September 1949, after a split in the Dravidar Kazhagam, by:
n39b258d6922.x: Annadurai formed the DMK in 1949; Periyar had formed the Dravidar Kazhagam from the Justice Party in 1944. The DMK came to power in 1967.

ncd49702f7ff.s: A.K. Gopalan is associated with which satyagraha?
ncd49702f7ff.x: A.K. Gopalan is listed with Guruvayur; T.K. Madhavan, K.P. Kesava Menon and K. Kelappan were associated with Vaikom.

nb722a2c04d8.x: Ambedkar wrote Annihilation of Caste, Who Were the Shudras? and The Untouchables; Nimna Jatula Charitra was by Jala Rangaswamy.

na3d3c47a5b8.s: Ambedkar's mass conversion to Buddhism at Deeksha Bhoomi, Nagpur on 14 October 1956 was accompanied by how many vows?
na3d3c47a5b8.x: The conversion at Deeksha Bhoomi on 14 October 1956 was accompanied by 22 vows, not 32.

n06ebbd7650a.s: Harichand Thakur was associated with the:
n06ebbd7650a.x: Harichand Thakur was associated with the Matua Namashudras of Bengal, not the Nadar movement.

nc912af55934.x: Ayyankali founded the Sadhu Jana Paripalana Sangham; Sri Narayana Guru founded the SNDP Yogam and Periyar led the Self-Respect Movement.

nea6942f1cf4.s: The SNDP Yogam was founded in:
nea6942f1cf4.x: The SNDP Yogam was founded in 1903; 1906 is the Depressed Classes Mission.

nindian-history-22-5.s: Who headed the women's section of the Satyashodhak Samaj?
nindian-history-22-5.x: Savitribai Phule headed its women's section; the Samaj was founded by Jyotiba Phule for Shudras and Ati-Shudras.

nindian-history-22-15.s: Jyotiba Phule, founder of the Satyashodhak Samaj (1873), belonged to which community?
nindian-history-22-15.x: Phule belonged to the Mali community and founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 to uplift the backward classes.

n541dda249fd.s: Periyar launched the Self-Respect Movement in:
n541dda249fd.x: The Self-Respect Movement began in 1925; the anti-Hindi agitation was in 1937, the Dravidistan demand in 1940 and the DMK in 1949.

n07574a9a572.x: Annamalai University was founded in 1929; the Andhra University Act and Madras Hindu Religious Endowments Act were of 1926.

nbe11fac944e.s: The journal 'Adi Hindu' was associated with:
nbe11fac944e.x: Adi Hindu was Bhagya Reddy Varma's journal; Jai Bheem and Veera Bharati were Jala Rangaswamy's papers.

ncc5dc95bdf2.s: Which of the following association–founder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Temperance and Social Purity Sangham – Kandukuri Veeresalingam
Social Purity Association – R. Venkataratnam Naidu
Varthamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samaj – Gidugu Ramamurthy
ncc5dc95bdf2.x: The Temperance and Social Purity Sangham was founded by Desiraju Peda Bapayya, not Veeresalingam.

nc59e16e899d.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
nc59e16e899d.s: Which was the first Telugu political journal?
nc59e16e899d.x: Chintamani was the first Telugu political journal; Satyaduta was the Bellary Christian Mission's, Satyasamvardhini the Rajahmundry Prarthana Samaj's, and Janana Patrika concerned women's education.

nce94984a84e.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: too few dated facts)
nce94984a84e.s: Bhandaru Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam at Brundavanapuram, Machilipatnam in:
nce94984a84e.x: Acchamamba founded the Stree Samajam in 1902.

ne0212d4a73c.s: Along with Gurajada Apparao, who led the Vyavaharika (spoken Telugu) movement?
ne0212d4a73c.x: Gidugu and Gurajada led the Vyavaharika cause to narrow the gap between written and spoken Telugu, while orthodox pandits backed Granthika.

n59bb3cf6b89.s: The first widow remarriage in Andhra, held at Veeresalingam's house in Rajahmundry, took place on:
n59bb3cf6b89.x: It took place on 11 December 1881 at Ananda Udyana Mandapam; the groom was Gogulapati Sriramulu and the bride Seethamma (Gauramma).

nc8f7267d012.s: The principal centres of the Brahmo movement in Andhra were Rajahmundry and:
nc8f7267d012.x: Rajahmundry and Kakinada were the main Brahmo centres in Andhra, where the movement peaked during 1870–1935.

ne7c58265ea6.s: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in:
ne7c58265ea6.x: The Madras Mahajana Sabha was formed in 1884; the Madras Native Association of Gajula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty dates to 1852.

n2b6ba630cf8.x: Gidugu was known as Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Pitamaha and Abhinava Vaganushasanudu and received Rao Saheb and Kaisar-e-Hind; Andhra Kesari is not his title.

n0d268f9ef27.s: Raghupathi Venkataratnam Naidu founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in:
n0d268f9ef27.x: He founded the Samajika Shuddhi Samajam in 1891 and was associated with the anti-nautch movement in Madras.

ne5c56645d84.s: Which Telugu journal was orthodox and opposed women's education?
ne5c56645d84.x: Andhra Bhasha Sanjeevani was orthodox and opposed women's education; Vivekavardhini attacked corruption and superstition and Satyasamvardhini printed a biography of Rammohan Roy.

n22a5fa4b860.s: The Telugu journal Janavani was associated with:
n22a5fa4b860.x: Janavani was associated with Tapi Dharma Rao; the monthly Telugu (1919) with Gidugu and the Andhra Sahitya Parishad magazine with Jayanti Ramaiah Pantulu.

n9f8d196aa5a.s: Gurajada Appa Rao's 'Mutyala Saralu' is noted for:
n9f8d196aa5a.x: Mutyala Saralu introduced a new metre; Kanyasulkam attacked bride-price and Desamunu Preminchumanna is his patriotic song.

n7afebe5fc52.s: Who was the first to render classical Sanskrit drama such as Abhijnana Sakuntalam and Ratnavali into Telugu?
n7afebe5fc52.x: Through translations of Abhijnana Sakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram and Ratnavali, Veeresalingam first rendered classical Sanskrit drama into Telugu.

n91c98e975a9.s: In Gurajada's Kanyasulkam, written in the Srikakulam dialect, which character is portrayed as a reformer?
n91c98e975a9.x: Soujanya Rao is the reformer, while Ramappa Pantulu is portrayed as a hypocrite.

nabaa563cbd8.s: The anti-remarriage work 'Stree Punarvivaha Durvada Nirvaranam' was written by:
nabaa563cbd8.x: Vedam Venkataraya Sastri wrote it; Paidah Ramakrishnayya supported remarriages at Kakinada and Kasibhatta Brahmayya Sastri was linked with the Aryananda Brundavani Sabha.

nap-history-15-12.s: The newspaper Andhra Geeta Svarajya, published from Madras, was started in 1921 by:
nap-history-15-12.x: Andhra Geeta Svarajya was started by Tanguturi Prakasam in 1921 and published from Madras.

nap-history-16-16.s: The journal Hasyavardhani was associated with:
nap-history-16-16.x: Hasyavardhani was Kokkonda Venkata Ratnam's journal; Veeresalingam was linked with the Brahmo Samaj in Andhra, Viveka Vardhini and the Vyavaaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samajam.

n9f8789cf81e.s: Who wrote Kanyasulkam, the satirical social play attacking bride-price and the plight of widows?
n9f8789cf81e.x: Kanyasulkam was written by Gurajada Apparao; Komarraju Lakshmana Rao founded the Sri Krishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam.

nap-history-15-3.s: Desha Matha, which strongly supported the Home Rule Movement, was edited by:
nap-history-15-3.x: Desha Matha was edited by Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham and backed the Home Rule Movement.

nap-history-15-11.s: Who was one of the founders and the first editor of the weekly Telugu magazine Krishna Patrika?
nap-history-15-11.x: Konda Venkatappayya was one of Krishna Patrika's founders and its first editor.

nbb0cb67b54a.x: Satyaraju Purvadesayatralu was based on Gulliver's Travels; Veeresalingam also wrote the first Telugu novel Rajasekhara Charitra and the satire Brahma Vivaham.

nc96c1ee7a2e.s: Which of the following did NOT reject idol worship or caste outright, unlike the Brahmo Samaj?
nc96c1ee7a2e.x: The Prarthana Samaj did not reject idol worship or caste outright, whereas the Brahmo Samaj took a categorical position against them.

n8648d9169cf.s: Gurajada's Kanyasulkam, written in 1890, was first staged in:
n8648d9169cf.x: Kanyasulkam was written in 1890, first staged on 13 August 1892 and published in 1897 by Vavilla.

n6589cc43704.s: Christian mission schools in Andhra admitted:
n6589cc43704.x: Mission schools admitted Sudras and Panchamas, extending education beyond the traditional upper-caste groups.

nd75198ff6ec.s: Which of the following pairs of Telugu work and author is correctly matched?
nd75198ff6ec.x: Seesari Charitra (1875), a rendering of Julius Caesar, is by Vavilala Vasudeva Sastri, who also wrote Nandaka Rajyam; Yayati Charitra is Ponnekanti Telaganaryudu's and Rajasekhara Charitram is Veeresalingam's.

n767c0e298bf.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: too few dated facts)
n767c0e298bf.s: C.P. Brown compiled his Telugu-English and English-Telugu dictionaries in:
n767c0e298bf.x: Brown, Collector of Cuddapah, compiled the dictionaries in 1853 and edited Nannaya, Tikkana and Pothana; 1815 is when Colin Mackenzie became Surveyor General.

n2f0c382031b.s: Benjamin Schultze's four Telugu books were printed in 1747 at:
n2f0c382031b.x: Schultze, of the Danish-Halle Mission, had his Telugu books printed at Halle in 1747; William Carey's Telugu Bible came from Serampore (1812-19).

n7b7f81c5863.s: Who helped Colin Mackenzie collect the Kaifiyats?
n7b7f81c5863.x: The Kavali brothers (Borraiah, Venkataramaiah, Lakshmaiah) helped Mackenzie, who became the first Surveyor General in 1815.

na46ddf15e76.s: Telugu Language Day, observed on 29 August, marks the birth anniversary of:
na46ddf15e76.x: Telugu Language Day on 29 August marks Gidugu's birth anniversary and is associated with Telugu Language Awards.

nd580da5246b.s: The 1912 and 1913 Rajahmundry sessions of the Andhra Sahitya Parishat were presided over by:
nd580da5246b.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam presided over the Rajahmundry sessions; the Parishat was founded at Madras in 1911 and later based at Kakinada.

nf8914f381ce.s: Who led the confederacy of the post-Kakatiya liberation movement?
nf8914f381ce.x: Prolaya Nayaka led the post-Kakatiya liberation confederacy.

na785d4ea8c2.s: During the early period of missionary activity, the major contribution to education in Andhra was made by:
na785d4ea8c2.x: Christian missionaries made the major contribution; the Adams Regulation and the Press Acts related to press control.

n20d6f7f0344.s: Which work is the standard answer for the first Telugu novel?
n20d6f7f0344.x: Veeresalingam's Rajasekhara Charitram is the standard answer, though some scholars propose Kokkonda Venkataratnam's Mahasweta.

n1b5e2fd0ed5.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the legal age of marriage in India?
o: The 2021 proposal to raise women's age to 21 had become law by January 2026
The 1978 amendment raised it to 18 for girls and 21 for boys
The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 prescribes 18 for women and 21 for men
In January 2026 the legal age for women remained 18
n1b5e2fd0ed5.x: The 2021 Cabinet proposal had not become law by January 2026, when the legal age for women remained 18.

n3deb5a2acb6.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Lex Loci Act (Caste Disabilities Removal Act), 1850?
o: It was passed under Lord Dalhousie
It barred converts from inheriting ancestral property
Orthodox Hindus saw it as an incentive to conversion
It became one of the grievances behind 1857
n3deb5a2acb6.x: The Act did the opposite: it let a Hindu who converted still inherit ancestral property.

n646f7fc8cda.s: Veeresalingam's second girls' school was established at Innispeta, Rajahmundry, in:
n646f7fc8cda.x: His first girls' school dates to 1874 and the Innispeta school to 1881; he was also the first in Andhra to promote co-education.

nc784b9bff43.s: Who founded the Social Service League at Bombay in 1911?
nc784b9bff43.x: N.M. Joshi founded the Social Service League; Kunzru founded the Seva Samiti (Allahabad, 1914) and Pandita Ramabai the Sharada Sadan (1889).

na3857d7a6e6.s: Jyotiba and Savitribai Phule opened a girls' school at Pune in:
na3857d7a6e6.x: The Phules opened the Pune girls' school in 1848 and a home for upper-caste widows in 1854; Savitribai is regarded as India's first woman teacher.

nfd6dc48c759.s: The Caste Disabilities Removal Act of 1850 is also known as the:
nfd6dc48c759.x: The Lex Loci Act protected a convert's right to inherit ancestral property; sati was dealt with by the 1829 Regulation.

n4901226d841.s: The Age of Consent Act, 1891, enacted under Lord Lansdowne, raised the age of consent for girls from 10 to:
n4901226d841.x: The 1891 Act raised the age of consent from 10 to 12 and regulated consummation rather than the age of marriage.

n82dbcc41e3c.s: The Native Marriage Act of 1872 fixed the minimum marriage age for girls at:
n82dbcc41e3c.x: The Act fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys, allowed inter-caste marriage and barred polygamy.

ne7bb8cbdf3b.s: Under the Sati Regulation (Regulation XVII of 1829) of William Bentinck, participation in sati was treated as:
o: A minor offence punishable by fine
ne7bb8cbdf3b.x: The Regulation made sati illegal and treated participation in it as culpable homicide.

n3f241ad56b2.s: Besides child marriage, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar campaigned against:
n3f241ad56b2.x: Vidyasagar campaigned against child marriage and polygamy; his work was not confined to widow remarriage.

n484a4a6d985.s: Pandita Ramabai founded the Arya Mahila Samaj at Poona in:
n484a4a6d985.x: The Arya Mahila Samaj was founded in 1882; Sarada Niketan in Guntur (1922) was founded by Unnava Lakshminarayana with his wife Lakshmibayamma.

nafd4aad85ef.s: In 1925 the age of consent in India was raised to:
nafd4aad85ef.x: The age of consent went from 10 to 12 in 1891, to 14 in 1925, to 16 in 1949 and to 18 in 2012 under POCSO.

n96e4dcb5ad4.s: Under POCSO/BNS, the age of consent in India is:
n96e4dcb5ad4.x: The age of consent is 18 under POCSO/BNS, while the PCMA 2006 fixes the minimum marriage age at 18 for women and 21 for men.

n7531d80bb59.s: Act V of 1843, which made slavery illegal in British India, was passed under:
n7531d80bb59.x: The Charter Act of 1833 directed abolition, Act V of 1843 under Ellenborough made slavery illegal, and the IPC of 1860 made the slave trade an offence.

nf695eb266eb.s: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act was enacted in July 1856 under:
nf695eb266eb.x: The bill was prepared under Dalhousie, but the Act was enacted in July 1856 under Canning; it legalised widow remarriage and legitimised the children.

ncbb3fbc0485.s: Bengal Regulations XXI of 1795 and III of 1804 declared ____ to be murder.
ncbb3fbc0485.x: These Regulations declared infanticide, including female infanticide, to be murder.

nb57e2cf146e.s: Bharat Stree Mahamandal, founded at Allahabad in 1910, was established by:
nb57e2cf146e.x: Sarala Devi Chaudhurani founded it in 1910; it is regarded as the first major all-India women's body founded by a woman.

o: A husband's suit for restitution of conjugal rights
n8816f2e7ade.x: Rakhmabai's husband Dadaji sued for restitution of conjugal rights after their child marriage, raising questions of consent and conjugal rights.

ncf628a8abc9.s: Which of the following pairs relating to Lord Lytton's rule is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Vernacular Press Act, 1878 – Restricted the Indian-language press
Arms Act, 1878 – Disarmed Europeans but exempted Indians
Second Afghan War, 1878–80 – Burden on Indian revenues
ncf628a8abc9.x: The Arms Act of 1878 disarmed Indians and exempted Europeans, not the reverse.

n187dedd5b59.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n187dedd5b59.s: Western education contributed to the growth of Indian nationalism by:
o: Reviving Persian as the court language
Helping English function as a link language
n187dedd5b59.x: Western education spread liberal ideas, made English a link language and created an educated middle class; it did not end racial discrimination.

n4119357d352.s: Surendranath Banerjee toured the country against the reduction of the ICS maximum age from 21 to:
n4119357d352.x: Banerjee, who passed the ICS in 1869 and was dismissed in 1874, campaigned against cutting the maximum age from 21 to 19.

n322539b23c1.s: The secretary of the Madras Native Association (1852) was:
n322539b23c1.x: Somasundaram Chettiyar was its secretary; P. Anandacharlu was secretary of the Madras Mahajana Sabha. Gazula Lakshmi Narasu Chetty was founder and first president.

n4ad3fcadad0.s: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's Anandamath (1882) is set against the background of the:
n4ad3fcadad0.x: Anandamath is set in the Sannyasi Rebellion; its song Vande Mataram was first sung at the INC by Tagore at Calcutta in 1896.

nef20de55c23.s: The early pre-Congress political associations were generally:
o: Regional bodies led by landlords or the urban elite
Equally representative of all sections of society
nef20de55c23.x: They were largely led by landlords or the urban elite and were regional in character.

n7e2c5b5e2be.s: When the Madras Mahajana Sabha was founded on 16 May 1884, its president was:
n7e2c5b5e2be.x: P. Rangaiah Naidu was president and P. Anandacharlu secretary; the Sabha demanded larger councils and more Indian representation.

nb06ea5fcea1.s: Which of the following was an unintended result of British rule that helped the growth of Indian nationalism?
o: End of racial discrimination in administration
nb06ea5fcea1.x: British rule unified India politically and administratively and linked it by railways, telegraph, post and uniform laws, while ruining many artisans.

n044bc505752.s: The demand for agricultural banks at Angalur in 1900 was made at a conference of the:
n044bc505752.x: Agricultural banks at Angalur were demanded at a Krishna District Association conference in 1900, not by the Madras Native Association.

n484f13214f8.shape: one-liner (sequence not possible: no dates in the facts)
n484f13214f8.s: Who called the safety-valve theory a 'colonial myth' and described Hume's role as a 'lightning conductor'?
n484f13214f8.x: Bipan Chandra used both expressions; R.P. Dutt saw the Congress as a conspiracy to head off a popular uprising.

nap-history-39-12.s: Who was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle?
nap-history-39-12.x: Nyapati Subba Rao was the first President of the Andhra Congress Circle; Govinda Rao Nanal was first President of the Hyderabad State Congress.

n867cc664290.s: A.O. Hume was demoted in 1879 after a clash with:
n867cc664290.x: Hume clashed with Lytton and was demoted in 1879; he retired in 1882 to Shimla and drew the idea of local self-government from Ripon.

ndbd8d3fd44b.s: P. Anandacharlu, the first Andhra President of the INC, presided over the session at:
ndbd8d3fd44b.x: Anandacharlu, a Chittoor delegate at the first session, presided at Nagpur in 1891; Kakinada 1923 was presided over by Maulana Mohammad Ali.

nc0408200a34.s: The Indian Association (1876) was founded by S.N. Banerjea and:
nc0408200a34.x: S.N. Banerjea and Ananda Mohan Bose founded the Indian Association; Mehta, Telang and Tyabji founded the Bombay Presidency Association (1885).

nap-history-39-4.x: T. Prakasam started Swarajya; Pattabhi Sitaramaiah wrote the History of the Indian National Congress.

nindian-history-123-5.s: Which session of the Indian National Congress saw the Moderate–Extremist split?
nindian-history-123-5.x: Surat 1907 saw the split; Lucknow 1916 brought the Lucknow Pact and the Extremists' return, and Nagpur 1920 adopted Non-Cooperation.

nindian-history-103-21.s: Who presided over the Allahabad session of 1888 as the first European President of the INC?
nindian-history-103-21.x: George Yule presided at Allahabad in 1888 as the first European President.

nindian-history-103-19.s: Which session of the INC debated the Nehru Report?
nindian-history-103-19.x: Calcutta 1928 debated the Nehru Report; Kanpur 1925 had Sarojini Naidu as the first Indian woman President and Ramgarh 1940 had Azad.

nc9a00760849.s: The British Indian Association was formed at Calcutta in 1851 by merging:
o: The Indian Association and the Landholders' Society
The Landholders' Society and the Bengal British India Society
The East India Association and the Bengal British India Society
The Brahmo Samaj and the Dharma Sabha
nc9a00760849.x: It merged the Landholders' Society (1838) and the Bengal British India Society (1843); the 1866 London body was Naoroji's East India Association.

nfc4ad77f6dc.s: Who presided over the Lucknow session of the INC in 1916?
nfc4ad77f6dc.x: Ambica Charan Mazumdar presided at Lucknow in 1916; R.C. Dutt presided at Lucknow in 1899 and Bonnerjee at Allahabad in 1892.

nd1720586cf5.s: How many times did Dadabhai Naoroji preside over the Indian National Congress?
nd1720586cf5.x: Naoroji presided three times; Surendranath Banerjee and Rash Behari Ghosh presided twice each and Pherozeshah Mehta once.

nindian-history-103-16.s: At which session was Swaraj declared the goal of the INC under Dadabhai Naoroji?
nindian-history-103-16.x: Calcutta 1906 declared Swaraj the goal under Naoroji; Benares 1905 was presided over by Gokhale and Surat 1907 saw the split.

n43d4c74264c.s: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress?
n43d4c74264c.x: W.C. Bonnerjee presided; Hume was General Secretary and Wedderburn and Justice John Jardine were British founding members.

n01f83736c27.s: The Poona Sarvajanik Sabha was founded on 2 April 1870 by M.G. Ranade and:
n01f83736c27.x: Ranade and G.V. Joshi founded it; in 1875 it petitioned the House of Commons for Indian representation in Parliament.

n4ddd3cfc869.s: Who presided over the Kakinada session of the INC in 1923?
n4ddd3cfc869.x: Maulana Mohammad Ali presided at Kakinada in 1923; Rash Behari Ghosh (1908), Bhupendranath Basu (1914) and M.A. Ansari (1927) presided at Madras.

nd556addfba7.s: Who presided over the Gaya session of the INC in 1922?
nd556addfba7.x: C.R. Das presided at Gaya in 1922; Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur 1925, Mudholkar at Bankipore 1912 and Azad at Ramgarh 1940.

nd3b4171f5c5.s: The only INC session presided over by Mahatma Gandhi was held at:
nd3b4171f5c5.x: Gandhi presided only at Belgaum in 1924, which reconciled the Swarajists and No-Changers.

n9be4335d5cb.s: Who was the first Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress?
n9be4335d5cb.x: Sarojini Naidu (Kanpur 1925) was the first Indian woman President; Annie Besant (Calcutta 1917) was the first woman President, and Nellie Sengupta presided at Calcutta in 1933.

nindian-history-103-3.s: Who presided over the Madras session of the INC in 1894?
nindian-history-103-3.x: Alfred Webb presided at Madras in 1894; Naoroji at Calcutta 1886, Sayani at Calcutta 1896 and Gokhale at Benares 1905.

n107d21447de.s: The Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) took place during the viceroyalty of:
n107d21447de.x: The Ilbert Bill came under Ripon; Lytton (1876-80) held the Delhi Durbar of 1877 and passed the Vernacular Press and Arms Acts in 1878.

na6b093a50fb.s: The first session of the INC (1885) was shifted from Poona to Bombay because of an outbreak of:
na6b093a50fb.x: The shift was due to cholera, not plague; the session met at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay, under Viceroy Dufferin.

nindian-history-103-7.s: Who presided over the Nagpur session of the INC in 1920?
nindian-history-103-7.x: C. Vijayaraghavachariar presided at Nagpur in 1920; Motilal Nehru at Amritsar 1919, C.R. Das at Gaya 1922 and Gandhi at Belgaum 1924.

nindian-history-102-11.s: Who presided over the Surat session of the INC in 1907?
nindian-history-102-11.x: Rash Behari Ghosh presided at Surat in 1907; Gokhale at Benares 1905 and Mazumdar at Lucknow 1916.

nindian-history-102-38.s: Who presided over the Haripura session of the INC in 1938?
nindian-history-102-38.x: Subhas Bose presided at Haripura in 1938; Gandhi at Belgaum 1924, Azad at Ramgarh 1940 and Pattabhi at Jaipur 1948.

nindian-history-102-13.s: Who presided over the Jaipur session of the INC in 1948?
nindian-history-102-13.x: Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided at Jaipur in 1948; Nehru at Faizpur 1936, Bose at Tripuri 1939 and Azad at Ramgarh 1940.

n955a8abd330.s: Who presided over the Madras session of 1887 as the first Muslim President of the INC?
n955a8abd330.x: Badruddin Tyabji presided at Madras in 1887; Naoroji presided at Calcutta 1886, Yule at Allahabad 1888 and Wedderburn at Bombay 1889.

naad38d58d50.s: Which pre-Congress body organised All-India National Conferences in 1883 and 1885?
naad38d58d50.x: The Indian Association, the most important pre-Congress body, organised these conferences and opposed the Arms Act and Vernacular Press Act.

n2060a0a5637.s: Kadambini Ganguly, who addressed the 1890 Calcutta session of the INC, was the first woman graduate of:
n2060a0a5637.x: Kadambini Ganguly was Calcutta University's first woman graduate and addressed the 1890 session presided over by Pherozeshah Mehta.

nc4543719da9.s: How many delegates attended the first session of the Indian National Congress?
nc4543719da9.x: The first session had 72 delegates, was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee and had A.O. Hume as General Secretary.

n304abbd6655.s: Gandhi made his first appearance on the Congress platform at the session of:
n304abbd6655.x: Gandhi first appeared at the 1901 Calcutta session under Dinshaw Wacha; Vande Mataram was first sung at Calcutta in 1896 under R.M. Sayani.

n5bdc6ca31de.x: Neel Darpan portrayed the oppression of indigo cultivators; Anandamath (1882) is the source of Vande Mataram.

n7c8c054f429.s: The name 'Indian National Congress' is credited to:
n7c8c054f429.x: The name is credited to Dadabhai Naoroji; Bonnerjee presided over the first session, and Hume's Indian (National) Union was one of its organisational origins.

ndd84c8565dd.s: The safety-valve theory was first mentioned in the 1913 biography of A.O. Hume written by:
ndd84c8565dd.x: Wedderburn's 1913 biography first mentioned it; Lala Lajpat Rai then used it in Young India (1916) to attack the Moderates.

n0898cfdf1bc.s: After the Surat split of 1907, the Extremists re-entered the Congress at the session of:
n0898cfdf1bc.x: Surat split the Congress and the Extremists re-entered at Lucknow in 1916; Calcutta 1906 had adopted Swaraj as the goal.

n6cb8528b233.s: Ponaka Kanakamma, the first Telugu woman to attend an INC session, led the women's wing at the session of:
n6cb8528b233.x: She led the women's wing at the Kakinada (Coconada) session of 1923, not Madras 1914.

n64a90df8b01.s: Who was the first president of the British Indian Association?
n64a90df8b01.x: Radhakanta Deb was its first president and Debendranath Tagore its secretary; the Madras Native Association began as its adjunct.

n67d042f6444.s: Dadabhai Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in:
n67d042f6444.x: Naoroji founded the East India Association in London in 1866.

nindian-history-102-14.s: The last INC session attended by Tilak was the session of:
nindian-history-102-14.x: Tilak last attended at Amritsar in 1919; the Extremists had returned at Lucknow in 1916 after the 1907 Surat split.

nindian-history-111-11.s: The Nehru Report was associated with:
nindian-history-111-11.x: Motilal Nehru chaired the Nehru Report committee; Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the Purna Swaraj resolution at Lahore.

nindian-history-103-10.s: Which was the first rural session of the Indian National Congress?
nindian-history-103-10.x: Faizpur (December 1936) was the first rural session; Karachi 1931 adopted the Fundamental Rights resolution and Nehru presided at Lucknow in April 1936.

nap-history-39-16.s: Continuous Congress rule in Andhra Pradesh was broken in 1983 by the:
nap-history-39-16.x: In 1983 the TDP ended continuous Congress rule in Andhra Pradesh; Congress(I) had been formed on 1 January 1978.

nindian-history-102-22.s: Which of the following was an early demand of the Indian National Congress?
o: Separation of the Executive and Judiciary
nindian-history-102-22.x: Separation of the Executive from the Judiciary was among the early Moderate demands, and formulating public demands was a founding objective.

nindian-history-102-16.s: Who was the Congress President at the time of Independence?
nindian-history-102-16.x: J.B. Kripalani was President in 1947; Azad held the presidency from the 1940 Ramgarh session until 1946.

nindian-history-102-35.s: Gandhi gave up his primary membership of the Congress in:
nindian-history-102-35.x: Gandhi resigned in 1934 and never formally rejoined, though he remained its guiding leader.

nindian-history-123-15.s: The 1931 Karachi session of the INC was presided over by:
nindian-history-123-15.x: Patel presided at Karachi in 1931; Nehru presided at Lahore 1929 and Faizpur 1936, and Bose at Haripura 1938.

nindian-history-123-7.s: The 1927 Madras session, associated with the boycott of the Simon Commission, was presided over by:
nindian-history-123-7.x: The 1927 session met at Madras under M.A. Ansari.

nap-history-39-9.s: T. Prakasam started the English daily Swarajya to spread the Congress message on:

nindian-history-102-10.s: After the Lahore session of 1929 adopted Purna Swaraj, which day was observed as Independence Day?
nindian-history-102-10.x: Following the Lahore resolution under Jawaharlal Nehru, 26 January 1930 was observed as Independence Day.

n21c85dea646.s: In the 'lightning-conductor' interpretation of the Congress's origin, Hume is seen as:
o: Creating an outlet for popular discontent
Shielding the young organisation from official hostility
Suppressing the Congress on Dufferin's orders
n21c85dea646.x: The lightning-conductor view sees Hume shielding the infant Congress from official suppression, whereas the safety-valve view sees it as an outlet for discontent.

nf1dbb2141b6.s: Regarding the formation of the INC, Lord Dufferin:
o: Founded it by an official proclamation in 1885
Opposed every proposal for a forum of educated Indians
Probably suggested an annual meeting of educated Indians, but did not demonstrably propose the INC
nf1dbb2141b6.x: Dufferin may have suggested an annual forum of educated Indians, but there is no proof that he proposed the INC itself.
